terms.definitionEn: The highest-level heading element, commonly used for the page's main heading.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر عنوان من أعلى مستوى، وغالبًا بيكون العنوان الرئيسي للصفحة.

terms.definitionEn: A block of prose expressing one related thought.
An element marking text as having great importance or urgency.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر بيوضح إن النص له أهمية قوية أو طابع عاجل.

terms.definitionEn: A spoken stress placed on a word or phrase to make its intended focus clear.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر بيضيف تشديد معنوي على كلمة أو جزء من الجملة.

terms.definitionEn: A container for items when their sequence carries no meaning.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر بيجمع عناصر قائمة ترتيبها مش مهم.

terms.definitionEn: An entry in an ordered or unordered collection, represented by one element.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر بيمثل بند واحد داخل قائمة مرتبة أو غير مرتبة.

terms.definitionEn: A section element for introductory content or navigation related to its surrounding region.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر لقسم تمهيدي أو روابط تنقل مرتبطة بالمنطقة اللي جواه.

terms.definitionEn: A section element containing the page's major links between locations.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر لقسم بيضم روابط التنقل الرئيسية.

terms.definitionEn: An element containing the document's dominant material, excluding repeated page-wide regions.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر بيضم المحتوى الأساسي للصفحة بعيدًا عن الأجزاء المتكررة زي التنقل.

terms.definitionEn: A self-contained composition that can make sense independently or be distributed separately.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر لمحتوى مستقل يقدر يتفهم لوحده أو يتنشر بشكل منفصل.

terms.definitionEn: A thematic grouping of content, typically identified by a heading.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر بيجمع محتوى عن موضوع واحد، وغالبًا بيكون له عنوان.

terms.definitionEn: A region for complementary content related to the surrounding page or article.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر لمحتوى جانبي أو مكمل مرتبط بالصفحة أو المقال المحيط.

questions.question: What is the usual semantic role of this element?
options: The page's primary heading
A paragraph of fine print
A navigation menu
A caption attached to an image
questions.explanation: h1 marks a top-level heading for the page or section.
questions.explanationAr: عنصر h1 بيمثل عنوانًا رئيسيًا للصفحة أو القسم.

questions.question: What kind of content does p represent?
options: A numbered list entry
A standalone paragraph
An emphasized word only
A page footer
questions.explanation: The p element represents a paragraph of text.

questions.explanation: The heading and paragraph display their text in separate blocks.
questions.explanationAr: العنوان والفقرة بيظهروا كنصين في كتلتين منفصلتين.

questions.prompt: Mark the sentence as a paragraph.
questions.explanation: The p element groups a paragraph.

questions.question: What meaning does strong add to this text?
options: It makes the text a hyperlink
It labels the text as a list item
It marks the instruction as important
It marks a citation from another source
questions.explanation: strong conveys strong importance; bold styling alone is not its defining meaning.
questions.explanationAr: strong بيوضح أهمية النص، مش مجرد شكل الخط.

questions.explanation: The em element marks stress emphasis, while the text remains visible.

questions.question: What structure does this markup describe?
options: Two paragraphs with numbering
A pair of navigation landmarks
One ordered list with nested headings
Two items in an unordered list
questions.explanation: ul groups list items whose order is not significant.
questions.explanationAr: ul بيجمع بنود قائمة ترتيبها مش أساسي.

questions.explanation: Each list item's text is rendered as a separate item.
questions.explanationAr: نص كل بند في القائمة بيظهر كبند منفصل.

questions.prompt: Choose the list container when the order of the items is not meaningful.
questions.explanation: An unordered list is appropriate when changing the order does not change the meaning.

questions.question: Why is nav appropriate for this region?
options: It declares a list with a required numeric order
It groups the page's major navigation links
It identifies one self-contained story
It defines the document's only visible heading
questions.explanation: nav identifies a significant group of navigation links.
questions.explanationAr: nav بيحدد مجموعة مهمة من روابط التنقل.

questions.prompt: Wrap the dominant content of the page in its main region.
questions.explanation: main contains the document's dominant content.

questions.question: What makes article a suitable element here?
options: It forces every child to become a heading
It creates a form submission boundary
It is the required parent of all paragraphs
The report is a self-contained composition
questions.explanation: article is suited to a self-contained composition that can stand on its own.
questions.explanationAr: article مناسب لمحتوى مستقل يقدر يتفهم لوحده.

questions.prompt: Mark the short related recommendation as complementary content.
questions.explanation: aside can mark complementary content related to its surrounding context.

questions.expectedOutput: Choose fresh leaves, not dried ones.
questions.explanation: em changes the emphasis, not the words presented to the reader.
questions.explanationAr: em بيغير التشديد في الكلام، مش الكلمات المعروضة.

questions.prompt: Use a thematic region for the schedule and identify it with a heading.
questions.explanation: section groups related thematic content, usually with a heading.

questions.question: What does em communicate beyond its typical italic appearance?
options: Stress emphasis that can change the sentence's intended meaning
A requirement that the enclosed word is a foreign language
A warning that the text must be hidden from assistive technology
A guarantee that the enclosed text is a hyperlink
questions.explanation: em represents stress emphasis; browsers commonly italicize it, but style is not the semantic purpose.
questions.explanationAr: em بيمثل تشديد معنوي، والمظهر المائل مش هو المعنى الأساسي.

questions.prompt: Complete a numbered sequence of steps and preserve each step as an item.
questions.explanation: ol expresses an ordered sequence, while li represents each step.

questions.question: Which element is intended for the page's dominant content?
options: header, since it introduces the page and appears before main in document order
main, which identifies the dominant page content
article, which must contain every other region
footer, since it follows the main region
questions.explanation: main marks the dominant content, while header and footer commonly contain introductory and closing material.
questions.explanationAr: main بيحدد المحتوى الأساسي، وheader وfooter غالبًا للمقدمة والخاتمة.

questions.prompt: Provide a page-level introduction and then a distinct main-content region.
questions.explanation: header introduces its surrounding page or section; main identifies the dominant content.

questions.question: How should heading levels and paragraphs be used to organize a readable document?
keyPoints: Headings express a hierarchy of sections
A heading level reflects structural nesting
Paragraphs group prose into readable units
Choose headings for meaning rather than default font size
questions.modelAnswer: Headings describe the hierarchy of a document, while paragraphs group related prose. Choose levels based on the content structure and use CSS, rather than heading levels, to control visual size.

questions.question: What is the semantic difference between strong and em?
keyPoints: strong indicates strong importance or urgency
They are not interchangeable merely because both can alter styling
Nesting can express different degrees or scopes of meaning
questions.modelAnswer: strong marks content as especially important, while em marks stress emphasis within a sentence. Browsers often style them differently, but their meaning—not their default appearance—is the key distinction.

questions.question: When would you choose ul rather than ol for a collection of items?
keyPoints: ul is for items without meaningful sequence
Each item is represented by li
Visual marker style can be changed independently
questions.modelAnswer: Use ul when the items form a group but their sequence is not meaningful. Use ol when order matters, such as steps, and represent each entry with li.

questions.question: Why choose semantic page-region elements instead of using div for every region?
keyPoints: Elements provide structure to maintainers and tools
div remains useful when no semantic element fits
questions.modelAnswer: Semantic elements communicate the purpose of regions to browsers, assistive technology, and people maintaining the page. A div is still useful as a generic container when no more meaningful element applies.
